explanation: The statement is about two of the library's own definitions. `D` is the set `{z | |z.re| ≤ 1/2 ∧ 1 ≤ ‖z‖ ∧ 0 < z.im}` and `r y = √(1 - y²)`. The lemma says that the point `⟨-r y, y⟩` is in `D` when `√3/2 ≤ y ≤ 1`. All of its content comes from these local definitions and the local lemmas `mk_mem_D`, `h_r` and `r_le_half`. Mathlib has its own fundamental domain (`ModularGroup.fd`), but that set lives on the upper half-plane type `ℍ`, not on `ℂ`, and Mathlib has nothing about a point parametrised as `⟨-√(1-y²), y⟩`. I only read the definitions of `D`, `mk_mem_D` and `r` in the library file; I did not run a separate search of Mathlib, because the statement depends entirely on the library's own definitions.
